_purpose: Allowlist for boundary-parity.test.ts's item-1(c) TUI keybinding-producibility check. An entry here is a normalized key token bound in packages/arbor-tui/src/default-catalog.ts that packages/arbor-tui/src/input-terminal.ts's decodeTerminalInput/navigationKeyFromChar cannot reproduce from any raw terminal byte sequence, reviewed and accepted as reachable only via some other route (e.g. a genuinely GUI/host-specific key the terminal CAN deliver but this repo's decoder does not yet decode, or a documented palette-only mnemonic). A bound token that is NOT listed here and is not raw-producible is a live finding: audit/2026-08-23-50-defects.md WA-24/WA-25 are the exact defect shape this check exists to catch (a bound key that can never actually fire).
_findings_left_unlisted_on_purpose: This lane's investigation of input-terminal.ts confirmed decodeTerminalInput/navigationKeyFromChar can only ever produce: single printable characters, shift+<a-z> (via an uppercase byte), ctrl+<a-z> minus ctrl+i/j/m (bytes 0x09/0x0a/0x0d stay text — Tab/Enter/CR own that context), the eight CSI table names (up/down/left/right/pageup/pagedown/home/end), and enter/escape. default-catalog.ts binds several tokens outside that set (ctrl+shift+* combinations, ctrl+;, alt+y) with no evidence in this codebase that any of them is reachable another way (e.g. no command-palette invoke-by-selection path was found in update.ts/overlays.ts — the help overlay is read-only reference text, not a dispatchable list). This lane did not have authorization to unilaterally declare those bindings intentional, so they are left UNLISTED: boundary-parity.test.ts's real-tree assertion is expected to fail/report them until an operator reviews each one (fix the decoder, drop the binding, or add a reviewed entry here with a real reason).
